training_data: North American ADNI, 1,314 subjects, randomly halved into an SVM training half and a validation half used to fine-tune hyperparameters (BAAD: VBM + RBF-SVM; SVMst and SVMcog)
test_data: AIBL (n=519, Australia), J-ADNI (n=592, Japan), MIRIAD (n=69, UCL Dementia Research Centre, UK) and OASIS (n=128, USA)
reason: Both SVMs were trained and tuned only on North American ADNI. They were then applied to four cohorts from other consortia and countries, with the ADLS > 0.5 cut-off fixed in advance (Table 3: AD/NL accuracy 88.0-94.2% for SVMst, 92.5-100% for SVMcog). A fixed model on external cohorts is V4. Figure 5 also shows cohort-specific optimal cut-offs, but Table 3 uses the fixed 0.5 cut-off, and AUC is threshold-free. MCI-progression prediction was assessed in the ADNI validation half and as a pMCI-vs-NL comparison in J-ADNI.

quotes.quote: We randomly selected half from the total 1,314 subjects of AD neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) from North America for SVM training, and the remaining half were used for validation to fine-tune the model hyperparameters.

further evaluated it in test datasets involving 519, 592, 69, and 128 subjects from the Australian Imaging, Biomarker & Lifestyle Flagship Study of Aging (AIBL), Japanese ADNI, the Minimal Interval Resonance Imaging in AD (MIDIAD) and the Open Access Series of Imaging Studies (OASIS), respectively.

The performance was recalculated with the cuttoff value of ADLS > 0.5 because the optimal cut-off value for AD diagnosis of ADLS in the NA-ADNI database was 0.48, and the results are summarized in Table 3. The classification accuracy was ranged from 88.0 to 94.2% and 92.5 to 100% for SVMst and SVMcog, respectively.
